answer: To raise the cost of sybil floods, every new agent must first weave a continuous verification thread of at least 40 peer-attested micro-tasks whose behavioral signature is cross-checked by a rotating falcon auditor against a public knoll of historical interaction graphs. An attacker seeking N identities must therefore produce N distinct, non-colliding threads; the compute and attestation cost scales roughly as 40N plus graph-matching overhead, while an honest agent pays only its own ongoing activity.
